text:
A: Hello, love! Can you hear me? I'm Joanne, I'm in Gosport.
B: Yeah, hear you fine. Tracey, Sittingbourne.
A: Oh, Kent. I nearly said when I saw your picture, you remind me of my sister Michelle. Sorry, is that a strange thing to say?
B: No, it's alright. You remind me of me mum, to be honest, so we're even.
A: Oh, well, I'll take that! Erm, what do you do, Tracey?
B: Shelf stacking. Supermarket, early mornings. Up at quarter past four, start at five, done at eleven.
A: Quarter past four! Oh my goodness. I'm in a school kitchen, a primary, and I think I'm hard done by getting in for half seven.
B: School dinners? Me mum did school dinners. Years of it.
A: Did she really? Oh, it's hard graft, isn't it, people don't realise. It's not just dishing up. You're doing the prep, you're watching for allergies, there's always one who's crying 'cause his yoghurt's the wrong colour, and then you're on your hands and knees wiping the hall down after. My knees aren't what they was.
B: That's what Mum used to say. She'd come home and put her feet up on the pouffe and you wasn't allowed to talk to her for half an hour.
A: Ha! I'd like a rule like that. Is she still going, your mum?
B: Yeah. Bit forgetful now. I'm the one taking her to all her appointments. My sister's always "busy".
A: Oh, love. I know that one. I looked after my mum at the end, she had a long illness, and erm, it was mostly me as well. Michelle helped where she could, but. You know.
B: Yeah. Someone always ends up doing it.
A: They do. Sorry, that's a bit heavy for three minutes, isn't it? I don't know if that's what you wanted.
B: You're alright. Better than talking about the weather.
A: Well, the weather's lovely on the seafront today, actually, if you did want to! I try and get a little walk in at Stokes Bay when it's kind.
B: I walk the dog round the rec most days. Roxy. Staffie. She's slowing down, hips are going.
A: Oh bless her. I've got a cat, Biscuit, he's elderly too. Fussy as anything. I bought a different brand of pouches from Asda 'cause it was on offer and he just sat and looked at it like I'd insulted him.
B: Roxy'd eat the pouch and all.
A: Ha! Do you get away much? Holidays and that?
B: Caravan at Leysdown or Camber. Tenerife if we've got the money. Been four times.
A: Four times! I've only been abroad the once, Benidorm when I was twenty-four. Now it's a caravan in Dorset with Michelle, that's me. I get in a right state about the trains.
B: Just drive.
A: I don't drive, love! That's half the problem. Erm, what did you make of that puzzle at the beginning?
B: Gave up. Told the woman I had before, she finished it with a minute to spare.
A: Oh, I didn't finish it either. I felt a bit thick, to be honest.
B: You ain't thick. It was just a daft puzzle.
A: Thank you, that's kind. What do you do Friday nights? Mine's fish and chips, my one treat.
B: Chinese. Every week.
